thread:
anita: Heads up — we need temp access for a SIEM export triage. KMS-wrapped raw logs in s3://redwood-siem-raw. Who's ok with a JIT access pattern for 1h scoped to a ticket? cc @lee @mike-secops :eyes:
lee: +1 to JIT. Prefer creating a short-lived AssumeRole (sts:AssumeRole) with condition aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent and a 1h TTL. Audit trail via CloudTrail and an entry in the security audit index.
mike-secops: Before we carve access, what's the retention/derivative copy policy here? We should avoid copies that extend retention or bypass redaction. Exports must go through the scrub pipeline.
jordan: For this incident we need full raw lines for root cause — scrub pipeline will run afterwards and produce a redacted snapshot for the SIEM. Can we ensure the raw snapshot is timeboxed and access-revoked automatically?
lee: Implementation sketch: create role redwood-siem-jit-<ticket>, policy scoped to the exact S3 prefix + kms:Decrypt on the CMK. Attach condition: "aws:RequestTag/ticket" == "INC-12345" and "sts:ExternalId" maybe. Example IAM snippet:
```
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["s3:GetObject"],
      "Resource": ["arn:aws:s3:::redwood-siem-raw/path/to/snapshot/*"]
    },
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["kms:Decrypt"],
      "Resource": ["arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111122223333:key/abcd-ef01-2345-6789"]
    }
  ]
}
```
lee: Role lifetime 1h. A Lambda or ops-bot will revoke by removing the AssumeRole trust after TTL; record revocation event in the ticket.
mike-secops: We also need an export gating check so third-party analysts can't pull raw objects out. Suggest forcing copy -> scrub -> signed URL delivered to analyst, and flag in DLP if any PII remains.
anita: Agreed. For this triage: plan is create ticket INC-12345, generate snapshot, attach SR to ticket, spin up ephemeral role, analyst assumes role via sts:AssumeRole with MFA, pulls snapshot into ephemeral workstation (no persistent copy allowed), then we run scrub pipeline and push redacted artifacts to SIEM ingestion S3.
jordan: Small ops question — how do we prove KMS decrypts were done only via the proxy service (not by user keys)? We should ensure kms:ViaService condition or use an intermediate key policy that restricts decrypt to the log-proxy role.
mike-secops: Yes — update CMK key policy to restrict Decrypt to the log-proxy principal and the temporary role, and make sure CloudTrail is logging kms:Decrypt events to the security audit bucket (w/ Object ACLs locked down).
ops-bot: Incident workflow step created: INC-12345 -> jira:SEC-9123. Ephemeral role redwood-siem-jit-INC-12345 provisioned (pending manual approval).
anita: Approval given. Lee — can you add the 24h auto-revoke lambda and the CloudTrail alert rule for kms:Decrypt anomalies?
lee: On it. I'll push a PR with the role template and the revoke lambda. PR will include the policy and the CloudWatch alert rule. ETA 2h.
mike-secops: Also add a one-line radio log to the ticket stating: "No copies retained outside scrub pipeline; access window 1h; CMK usage logged". We'll need signoff from compliance.
anita: I'll ping compliance after PR merge. Thanks all :thumbsup:
